chapter: Swing, singers, Ed Fox and recordings
title: The Yeah Man and Billie Holiday

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Were you at any sessions in New York?
No, I never made a session. I used to -- most of the time, Walter Fuller and I used to hang out at the 'Yeah Man.'
The Yeah Man. That's where Billie Holiday was signing. She started out, her uncle was playing banjo and the guitar. Boy, and that chick used to -- boy, she used to kill us. We was there every night.
Her uncle. Or her father? Her father was Clarence Holiday.
I don't know, could have been her father.
He played guitar and banjo with Fletcher Henderson.
Yeah. Well, it must have been her father, then. Boy, man, me and Walter Fuller was there every night.
You and Walter Fuller were pretty good friends?
Oh, yeah. Fact, me and Walter and George Dixon, well, quite naturally Louis Taylor and Wallace Bishop, we was all --
Did you visit each other's houses, and things like that?
